title: Signing a CSR Using the Active Directory Certificate Services

blocks.text: When you configure a custom intermediate root certificate for SSL/TLS Inspection, you must generate and download a certificate signing request (CSR) in the Zscaler Admin Console, then send the CSR to a certificate authority (CA) for signing. Ensure that the CSR is signed as a subordinate CA or intermediate CA.

The following configuration example shows how the CSR can be signed using the Active Directory Certificate Services using Certreq.exe. To learn more about Certreq, refer to the Microsoft documentation.

blocks.item: Generate a certificate signing request. To learn more, see Generating Certificate Signing Request (CSR) for SSL/TLS Inspection. For this example, the downloaded file is named zscalerdemo.csr.
Enter cmd in the search bar.
A dialog prompt appears asking if you want to run the program as an administrator. Select Yes to open an elevated command prompt.
From the dialog box, select the desired certificate authority.

The issued certificate can be saved as zscalerdemo.cer so long as you have domain administrator access permissions. Go to the certificate that you saved and change the certificate file name so it has a .pem extension. For example, zscalerdemo.pem. The Zscaler service only accepts certificates with the .pem extension.
